answer_text:
"**A Whiter Shade of Pale**" was first sung by **Gary Brooker**, the frontman of the English rock band **Procol Harum**. "A Whiter Shade of Pale" was issued as Procol Harum's debut record on **12 May 1967**.

With its Bach-derived instrumental melody, soulful vocals, and melancholic tone, the music was composed by Gary Brooker and Matthew Fisher, while the lyrics were written by Keith Reid.

An enthusiastic response from listeners of the pirate radio station Radio London prompted Deram Records to rush-release the single on May 12, 1967. It was an instant worldwide success, reaching No. 1 on the UK Singles Chart for six weeks and the same spot in eleven countries.

In 1977, the song was named joint winner (along with Queen's "Bohemian Rhapsody") of "The Best British Pop Single 1952–1977" at the Brit Awards. The song was also inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 1998 and into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2018.

Sadly, Gary Brooker, whose soaring vocals on the band's 1967 proto-prog rock classic helped make the song a mainstay of 1970s FM radio, died on February 19, 2022, of cancer.
